entries.title: Integers on the number line
entries.explanation: Integers are whole numbers, their negatives, and zero. On a number line, zero is in the middle, positive integers go right and negative integers go left.
entries.worked_example: A point 4 units to the left of 0 is at -4.

entries.title: Opposites
entries.explanation: Opposites are the same distance from zero, on different sides. Keep the number and change its sign.
entries.worked_example: The opposite of 9 is -9, and the opposite of -2 is 2. Zero is its own opposite.

entries.title: Absolute value is a distance
entries.explanation: The absolute value of a number is its distance from zero, so it is never negative.
entries.worked_example: |-6| = 6 and |6| = 6, because both are 6 units from zero.

entries.title: Compare by position
entries.explanation: On a number line, numbers get greater to the right. A number farther left is less, even when its digits look bigger.

entries.title: Adding integers
entries.explanation: Same signs: add the distances and keep the sign. Different signs: subtract the distances and keep the sign of the number farther from zero.
entries.worked_example: -9 + 4: 9 - 4 = 5, and -9 is farther from zero, so -9 + 4 = -5.

entries.title: Adding the opposite
entries.explanation: To subtract an integer, add its opposite.

entries.title: The sign of a product
entries.explanation: Multiply the distances first, then decide the sign: same signs give a positive product, different signs give a negative product.
entries.worked_example: (-3) x 7: 3 x 7 = 21, and the signs are different, so the product is -21.

entries.title: The sign of a quotient
entries.explanation: Divide the distances first, then use the same sign rules as multiplication.
entries.worked_example: (-35) / (-5): 35 / 5 = 7, and the signs are the same, so the quotient is 7.

entries.title: Order of operations
entries.explanation: Work inside grouping symbols first, then multiply and divide from left to right, then add and subtract from left to right.

entries.title: Signed changes
entries.explanation: Rise, gain and deposit are positive changes. Fall, loss and withdrawal are negative changes. Add the change to the starting value.
entries.worked_example: A diver at -5 m rises 3 m: -5 + 3 = -2, so the diver is 2 m below the surface.
